title: Equations with x on both sides: balance them out
examples: What do you do when x is on both sides?
Which side should the x terms go on?

left.label: 3x
left.ask: Why take x off both sides?

explain.say: Look at this balance. On the left: 3x and 1. On the right: x and 5. It is level, so 3x plus 1 equals x plus 5. There are x boxes on both sides. Tricky! Let us tidy it up step by step.

draw.text: Equations with x on both sides: balance them out

left.label: 3x
left.ask: Why take x off both sides?

explain.say: Look at the single x on the right. Take one x off both sides. Then the left has 2x and 1, and the right has just 5. Will the scale stay level?

left.label: 3x
left.ask: Why take x off both sides?

explain.say: Yes, still level! Now 2x plus 1 equals 5. Look at the 1 on the left. Take 1 off both sides. What is left on each side?
Now 2x balances 4. Two boxes weigh 4, so cut both sides in half. One x weighs 2. So x is 2!
Great work! Check: 3 times 2 plus 1 is 7, and 2 plus 5 is 7. Level! Wow: the numbers on the boxes were the hidden weights all along. Challenge: solve 5x plus 2 equals 2x plus 11.

left.label: x
left.ask: How do you check the answer?

faq.q: Why take x off both sides?
faq.a: To get all the x boxes on one side. Take away the smaller number of x terms from both sides, so the x terms stay positive.
asks: How do you get rid of x on one side?

faq.a: To leave the x terms on their own. Taking 1 from both sides keeps the scale level and gives 2x equals 4.
asks: How do you get 2x on its own?

faq.q: How do you check the answer?
faq.a: Put your answer into both sides. If x is 2, the left is 3 times 2 plus 1, which is 7, and the right is 2 plus 5, which is also 7.
asks: How do I check an equation with x on both sides?

faq.q: How do you solve 5x plus 2 equals 2x plus 11?
faq.a: Take 2x off both sides: 3x plus 2 equals 11. Take 2 off both sides: 3x equals 9. Divide by 3: x is 3.

faq.q: Which side should the x terms go on?
faq.a: Either side works, but it is easiest to move them to the side with more x, so you never get a negative number of x.
asks: Should x go on the left or right?

facts: Doing the same thing to both sides keeps an equation true.
For 3x + 1 = x + 5, the solution x = 2 makes both sides equal 7.

quiz.why: Take x off both sides: 3x plus 3 equals 12. Take 3: 3x equals 9. So x is 3.

wrong.1: 5 adds 3 instead of taking it away.
wrong.2: 9 is 3x. You still need to divide by 3.

quiz.say: What is a good first step for 7x minus 4 equals 2x plus 6?
quiz.why: Taking 2x from both sides puts all the x terms on the left: 5x minus 4 equals 6.

wrong.1: Adding 7x puts more x on both sides.
wrong.2: Dividing by 2 makes fractions and does not collect the x terms.
